claims.text: A Co-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ni multi-principal-element alloy processed by severe plastic deformation and low-temperature annealing will develop a dual-phase microstructure.
The proposed dual-phase microstructure will maximize hardness.
The proposed processing and microstructure will maintain or maximize alloy density.
The processed alloy will form a protective oxide layer that improves corrosion resistance.
The as-cast alloy is expected to have a coarse-grained microstructure.
The annealing temperature must be below the solvus of the secondary phase and above the recovery temperature.
An annealing range of 400°C to 600°C satisfies the relevant processing window for the proposed alloy.
Severe plastic deformation with strain greater than 4 will produce a nanocrystalline grain structure.
Severe plastic deformation will produce a high dislocation density.
Annealing after severe plastic deformation will precipitate a secondary sigma or Laves phase.
The precipitated secondary phase will impede dislocation motion.
The precipitated secondary phase will impede oxygen diffusion.
Grain refinement and increased dislocation density caused by severe plastic deformation will increase hardness.
The annealing-induced secondary phase will pin grain boundaries.
High-temperature exposure will form a dense, adherent Cr2O3 or Al2O3 scale that improves oxidation resistance.
Exceeding the secondary-phase solvus will dissolve the secondary phase and eliminate its strengthening effect.
The processed alloy will have more than 30% higher hardness than the as-cast alloy.
The processed alloy will have a density greater than 7.5 g/cm³.
The processed alloy will exhibit more than a 50% reduction in aqueous corrosion rate.
The processed alloy will retain oxidation resistance at temperatures up to 800°C.

contradictions.description: The example composition contains Co, Cr, Fe, Mn, and Ni but no Al, whereas the mechanism proposes Al2O3 as a possible protective scale without specifying any aluminum addition.

The prediction requires a hardness increase greater than 30%, but the falsification rule uses a greater-than-10% hardness criterion; an outcome between 10% and 30% would fail the stated prediction without falsifying it under the rule.
